topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing by introducing the lecturer, setting the lecture within the course, and outlining key learning objectives on cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Factors, Environment, and the 'Bad Luck' Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and evaluate whether its development is primarily governed by intrinsic biological chance or preventable environmental exposures.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study of pathogen interplay and chromosomal translocation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens damage DNA, emphasizing metabolic activation, adduct formation, and reactive intermediates.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Two-Stage Carcinogenesis, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish tumor promoters and chronic inflammatory microenvironments from direct mutagens, analyzing two-stage carcinogenesis and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the complementary genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify and prove the carcinogenicity of environmental agents.

topics.label: Closing Framing and Risk-Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing for the lecture, summarizing key takeaways and framing cancer prevention around individual and societal risk-benefit decisions.
